title: a release built from a warm cache kept an older day's security-upgrade layer
note: basis 'shown' means shown by the card's unit tests (failing on master c3a5b2b2, passing on the branch) and by make -n; no image was built here (no Docker daemon in the session); the walk (7159322336) showed an uncached build passing the gate.

findings.claim: the release path built trialbox-py (and on it -backup, -jvm, -embed) and the demo image with the build cache, so the unpinned apt-get upgrade layer could come from an older day and ship libzstd1 1.5.7+dfsg-1 (CVE-2026-124851); make release-images, ahead of the gates in make release-bundle, now pulls every digest-pinned outside base and then builds all six images with --no-cache and without --pull (which would send FROM trialbox-py to a registry); make images (dev) keeps its cache

nothing in the gates held the security-upgraded packages to the fixed version; deploy/images.lock security_floors now records libzstd1 and zlib1g for the five upgraded images and the release gates refuse an image whose SBOM has an older version or none (tools/supply_chain/floors.py, dpkg version order), and fail closed on a lock without floors

the local security-scan match in eval/bakeoff/results/2026-10-25/predictions_*.csv line 697 does not reproduce on the committed files with the locked scanner (0 findings with every plugin on); the scan reads the working tree, and tools/bakeoff_live.py writes predictions_*.csv into its --out folder, so a local re-run (or a scanner outside the lock) is the likely difference from CI
